turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can you help me think through weekend plans? I'm pretty introverted, so nothing too overwhelming — a quiet dinner or a walk sounds ideal.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Sure, a low-key weekend it is. A quiet dinner or a nature walk both sound relaxing.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Exactly, I need the recharge time.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Just got back from my friend's birthday, I ended up being the one DJing and getting everyone dancing until 2am, it was amazing.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Sounds like a great night! Did you know a lot of people there?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Half the room, honestly. I love being the center of attention at parties like that.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Oh, unrelated -- I got my sister's old car last month, a blue Honda Civic.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Nice, congrats on the new (to you) car -- a blue Honda Civic.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Help me plan something fun for my birthday next month.

probe_queries: What kind of birthday plan would Devon enjoy?

needle_probes.question: What car did Devon get from his sister?

annotation.tension: Devon explicitly self-labels as introverted and wanting low-key plans in session 1, then describes loving being the life of a large, loud party in session 2. Both are stated with equal confidence and no acknowledgment of tension between them.
annotation.why_unresolved: People genuinely contain both traits depending on context (recharge alone vs. thrive at a specific kind of social event) — flattening this into a single label is itself a plausible failure mode.
annotation.good_response_looks_like: Asking what kind of birthday vibe Devon's going for this time, or offering a range that could suit either quiet or high-energy plans, rather than assuming only one trait applies.
failure_modes_to_watch_for: Confidently plans only a quiet, low-key event, discarding the party evidence.
Confidently plans only a large loud party, discarding the introversion statement.
Invents a personality explanation not given by the user (e.g., 'Devon is an ambivert who alternates weekly').
